tagline: The open source AI coding agent, in your browser
description:
OpenCode is an open source AI coding agent. This package runs
OpenCode 2.2.3 (opencode serve --service) on your ZimaOS box,
with your projects mounted at /workspace.

Locally, open it on port 4096. From outside your network, do not
forward the port on your router: this app enables OpenCode's
remote access, so run `opencode pair --remote` inside the
container to print a one-time OpenTunnel link (and QR code) to
connect a browser or app. Links work once and expire within
minutes. Set OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD when installing.
author: restuindrawan

tips.before_install:
Set OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD during install. This app publishes
OpenCode through OpenTunnel (opencode pair --remote), and
OpenCode can run shell commands and edit files in /workspace,
so anyone who can reach it without the password or a one-time
pair link gets remote code execution in the container.

After install: give the tunnel a minute to set up on first
start, then run this in the container (ZimaOS container
terminal, or SSH): opencode pair --remote
It prints a one-time link and QR code to connect from outside.
Links work once and expire within minutes; run it again for a
new one. Locally you can also open http://<zima-ip>:4096.
If you left the password empty, a random one was generated and
saved; read it with: opencode service get password

Your provider API keys and sessions are stored in the data
folder (/root/.local/share/opencode, including auth.json), and
the service password and tunnel route in the config folder.
Keep both private. Adjust the /workspace path during install
to point at the projects you want OpenCode to work on.

Note: the upstream image is minimal (OpenCode and ripgrep, no
git or language toolchains), so tasks that need those tools
inside the container will be limited.

title: OpenCode
release_note: Fix v2 startup. Replace the removed `web --hostname/--port` command with `serve --service` on 0.0.0.0:4096, enable OpenTunnel remote access, and save OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD as the service password. Use `opencode pair --remote` in the container for one-time outside links.
